{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Proper one-point bandits with smooth strongly convex losses on known convex bodies\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{ONX\_\allowbreak{}BCO1\_\allowbreak{}SMOOTH\_\allowbreak{}STRONG\_\allowbreak{}PROPER}



Online learning and bandits



Expected static regret with exact bounded one-point feedback, feasible actions, and explicit domain conditioning and curvature budgets.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap; Other quantified gap



\textbf{Gap classes present.} Logarithmic gap; Other quantified gap



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Online regret minimization; task family: Online bandit



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Strongly convex; smoothness: Lipschitz gradient



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} derivative order: Order 0; feedback quality: Exact; operation: Played point loss value; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize expected static regret for proper one-point adversarial bandit convex optimization on a known compact convex body, allowing boundary comparators.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


The public domain belongs to \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal K_d=\{K:(4d)^{-1}B_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq B_2^d,\ K\text{ compact and convex}\}}. Every loss is the restriction of a continuously differentiable function on a neighborhood of \AtlasInlineMath{K}, takes values in \AtlasInlineMath{[0,1]} on \AtlasInlineMath{K}, is \AtlasInlineMath{\mu}-strongly convex, and is \AtlasInlineMath{\beta}-smooth in the Euclidean norm on \AtlasInlineMath{K}. No globally bounded strongly convex extension is assumed.



An oblivious adversary fixes the loss sequence before the learner seed is drawn. The domain is known, the losses are hidden, and \AtlasInlineMath{0<\mu\le\beta}. Only domains with a nonempty loss class are included. The family is nonempty exactly when \AtlasInlineMath{\mu\le32d^2}.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


At round \AtlasInlineMath{t}, play \AtlasInlineMath{X_t\in K}, incur \AtlasInlineMath{f_t(X_t)}, and observe exactly this scalar. No gradient, extra value query, or query outside \AtlasInlineMath{K} is available. The domain, horizon, and curvature budgets are public. Exact computations using the known domain are free; no additional loss information is included.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


The executed actions must be feasible almost surely at every round. The static comparator is the minimizer of the cumulative loss over the same domain and can lie on its boundary.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


\AtlasInlineMath{R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(X_t)-\min_{u\in K}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(u)}. The minimax risk is
\AtlasMath{\mathfrak R^*_{T,\mathrm{sc}}(d;\mu,\beta)=\sup_{K\in\mathcal K_d:\mathcal F(K;\mu,\beta)\ne\varnothing}\inf_A\sup_{f_{1:T}}\mathbb E_A R_T}
. The algorithm may depend on the known domain before the losses are selected.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


One exact scalar observation per round; the budget is the fixed horizon \AtlasInlineMath{T}. Geometric computation, internal arithmetic, and storage are not charged.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


All measurable randomized causal proper one-point policies are allowed. Computation on the known domain is unrestricted.




\AtlasMath{\sup_{f_{1:T}}\mathbb E_A R_T\le r}




The guarantee is uniform over admissible oblivious loss sequences for each public domain; the risk subsequently takes the worst admissible domain.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_horizon



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Euclidean dimension \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{T}: Horizon \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{T\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\mu}: Strong-convexity lower bound \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\mu\le32d^2}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\beta}: Gradient-Lipschitz upper bound \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\beta\ge\mu}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\kappa}: Condition number \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\kappa\ge1}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\kappa=\beta/\mu}



\AtlasInlineMath{K}: Known feasible convex body \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{(4d)^{-1}B_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq B_2^d}.



\AtlasInlineMath{R_b}: Radius used only to index the admissible ball lower-bound subclass \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R_b\in[(4d)^{-1},1]}.



\AtlasInlineMath{M_b}: Curvature scale of the ball lower-bound subclass \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<M_b<2}.



\AtlasInlineMath{M_b=\mu R_b^2}



\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_b}: Bounded-loss headroom on the lower-bound ball \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_b>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_b=1-M_b/2}



\AtlasInlineMath{Q_b}: Lower-bound scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{Q_b>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{Q_b=\min\{M_b,\Delta_b^2/M_b\}}
